_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Scoring the pitch against your criteria...

description: Use this for any recruiter pitch the user pastes in chat; use this, not intake_message, which is only the entry point for the form and attached files. It scores the pitch against the user's saved criteria and returns an evaluation_id, a composite score from 0 to 100, four sub-scores from 0 to 100 (relevance, specificity, cadence, spam where 100 is clean), flags, key reasons and a recommended action: interested, request_info or decline. It saves a cleaned summary and updates the sender scoreboard; the raw text is never stored. Input tips: send the whole pitch as message and sender_domain as a bare host such as stripe.com. A client that sends no user id has no desk: send criteria with the call, and the pitch is scored with nothing stored and an empty evaluation_id. Errors: no_desk means call set_criteria first with target_role, skills, salary_floor and remote_policy, then score again; no_user_id means send criteria. Never present a score from intake_message's sample profile as the user's real score. Pass the evaluation_id to draft_response to write a reply.

examples.message: Dear Candidate, you would be an awesome rockstar ninja for our client onsite in Dallas.

cadence_days.description: Optional days since the previous message from this sender, 0 to 365, such as 2. Used only for the cadence sub-score. Defaults to 7.

criteria.description: Optional criteria to score against instead of the desk's saved criteria, in the shape set_criteria takes. Needed when the client sends no user id (no ChatGPT sign-in and no OAuth connection): the pitch is then scored and nothing is stored.

dealbreakers.description: Optional, up to 20: constraints that rule out a pitch, such as ["Onsite required", "Legacy Java"]. Omit it or send [] for none.

remote_policy.description: Wanted work arrangement, such as "100% remote", "hybrid 1 day" or "any".

salary_floor.description: Minimum yearly base salary in whole US dollars, 0 to 10000000, such as 210000. Use 0 for no floor.

target_role.description: Target job title, such as "Staff Distributed Systems Engineer".

is_follow_up.description: Optional: true when this message follows up earlier outreach. Used only for the cadence sub-score. Defaults to false.

message.description: The full pitch text the user pasted, such as "Hi, we are hiring a Staff Engineer at Stripe, $220k base, remote."

previous_declined.description: Optional: true when the user already declined this sender. Used only for the cadence sub-score. Defaults to false.

sender.description: Optional sender email address, profile URL or domain, such as "jane@stripe.com". Used only when sender_domain is not given.

sender_domain.description: Optional sender domain as a bare host name, such as "stripe.com" (no @, no https://). It wins over sender. With neither, the domain is read from the message, else unspecified-sender.com.

name: score_message

as_of.description: Day of the call, as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

breakdown.description: The four sub-scores, each an integer from 0 to 100 where higher is better.

cadence.description: How well spaced the outreach is; low for rapid follow-ups or contact after a decline.

relevance.description: Fit with the target role, skills, salary floor and remote policy.

spam.description: Spam safety: 100 is clean, low means template tokens, buzzwords or urgency.

specificity.description: How concrete the pitch is: named company, role details and stated salary.

composite_score.description: Overall score from 0 to 100; 85 or more is a strong pitch.

evaluation_id.description: Id of this evaluation; pass it to draft_response. Kept for 30 days. Empty when nothing was stored because the client sends no user id.

flags.description: Warning flags. Values: missing_salary, dealbreaker_clash, token_failure (unfilled template token such as [Current Company]), aggressive_drip, repeat_after_decline, slop, artificial_urgency, free_webmail. Empty when the pitch is clean.

recommended_action.description: Suggested reply: interested, request_info or decline.

sender_domain.description: Sender domain the pitch is counted under on the scoreboard.

source.description: Where the data comes from: the user's own private desk.

summary.description: Short cleaned summary of the pitch with contact details removed; this is what is stored.

title: Score Inbound Pitch
